headline: Kanlaon Erupts, Then Emits Ash Twice as Alert Level 2 Holds
seoTitle: Kanlaon Erupts, Emits Ash as Alert Level 2 Holds
seoDescription: Kanlaon produced a brief explosive eruption on October 10 and two more ash emissions on October 11 while PHIVOLCS kept Alert Level 2.
deck: A brief explosive eruption sent ash five to six kilometers above the summit on Saturday; two lower ash plumes followed early Sunday.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Kanlaon Volcano produced a brief explosive eruption from 12:46 p.m. to 12:48 p.m. on October 10, sending an ash plume roughly five to six kilometers above the summit, according to PHIVOLCS and independent reports.
PHIVOLCS then recorded ash emissions at 1:28 a.m. and 5:15 a.m. on October 11. The plumes rose about 400 meters and 600 meters and drifted northwest and west, respectively.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: PHIVOLCS kept Kanlaon at Alert Level 2, indicating moderate volcanic unrest. The agency said continuing gas release can carry fine ash after the eruption opened a pathway through the vent.
Ashfall was reported in parts of Negros Occidental. Residents inside the four-kilometer permanent danger zone had already evacuated, and entry into that zone remains prohibited.

sections.heading: Why it matters to Filipinos
paragraphs: Ash can reduce visibility, irritate the eyes and lungs, contaminate water and affect crops and livestock. Communities downwind should follow PHIVOLCS and local-government instructions rather than rely on unverified social-media posts.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for additional PHIVOLCS bulletins, changes to the alert level, renewed explosive activity, wind-driven ashfall advisories and any expansion of evacuation or exclusion zones.

audit.verificationNotes: PHIVOLCS footage and statements support the eruption timing and plume height. GMA News and The Philippine Star independently corroborate the activity, Alert Level 2 and public-safety restrictions. The article does not claim that a larger eruption is imminent.
audit.duplicateCheck: The October 10 explosive eruption and October 11 ash emissions are independently newsworthy developments after earlier FMB reports on lower-level Kanlaon ash activity.

continuation.title: Kanlaon Emits 200-Meter Ash Plume; Alert Level 2 Remains
continuation.whatChanged: Kanlaon produced a new explosive eruption with a much higher ash column, followed by continuing ash emissions.
